ranking.note: Placed ahead of #26966 because the batching foundation it extracts is a stated prerequisite for the parallel-sync work

inconsistencies: Chain: #34489 (batch db writes) extracts foundation work for #26966 (parallel index sync); review #34489 first, as its batch boundaries and crash-recovery semantics determine whether the parallel version is safe.

#24230 and #35474 both push index decoupling toward multiprocess/test isolation (#24230 removes node internal types and cs_main from BaseIndex; #35474 moves index ownership out of globals into NodeContext). They will touch the same construction/lookup paths; decide the architecture in #24230 first so #35474 does not have to be redone.

#35229 converts CBlockIndex pointer parameters to references across indexing code, while #24230 aims to remove CBlockIndex from index interfaces entirely. The refactor may be moot or conflicting depending on #24230's direction; do not merge #35229 ahead of that decision.

#34132 and #35728 address the same underlying hazard: read/deserialization failures being reported as 'not found'. #35728 is the index-scoped fix (txindex/GetTransaction) and is the more in-category of the two; #34132 is mostly coins/dbwrapper (validation territory) with index queries as a consequence. Review #35728 first and check the two do not contradict each other on whether such a failure throws or is fatal.
result.notes: No bands were changed; the original single-PR assessments were already mutually consistent. The P2 group splits into two distinct efforts (framework decoupling #24230/#35474 and initial-sync performance #34489/#26966) plus one user-facing feature (#36002); the P3 group is error-reporting/integrity polish and housekeeping.
